chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah reported with an elevated chain (mursal), saying:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O son of Adam! If a bird were to eat your heart, it would not be satiated by it, and if the eye of a needle were placed upon your eye, it would cover it.

Do you intend with these two to recognise the kingdom of the heavens and the earth? If you are truthful, then here is the sun — a creation from the creations of God. So if you are able to fill your eyes from it, then it is as you say.

key_terms.بَصَرُكَ: Eyesight — used here as a symbol of human perceptual capacity
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: Technical hadith term: the narrator raised the chain, omitting intermediate transmitters (mursal/marfu')
key_terms.قَلْبَكَ: The heart — in Islamic tradition, the seat of intellect, desire, and spiritual perception
key_terms.مَلَكُوتَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: The kingdom/dominion of the heavens and earth — divine sovereignty over all creation

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about the limits of human intellect in knowing God?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses two striking analogies to demonstrate the absolute limits of human faculties — the heart's capacity for desire and the eye's physical limitation — as evidence against the rationalist claim that human intellect and perception suffice to comprehend the divine kingdom. The argument is addressed to those who believe they can know God's attributes through rational speculation alone, which this chapter forbids (al-kayfiyya). The challenge of gazing directly at the sun — itself a mere created thing — is posed as an irrefutable test of the claim.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah, raising it, said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O son of Adam<sup>as</sup>! If a bird was to eat your heart, it would not satiate it, and if a needle was to poke your eye, it would cover (blind) it.

You are intending with these two, to recognise the kingdoms of the skies and the earth? If you are truthful, so this here is the sun, a creation from the creations of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. So, if you are able to fill your eyes from it, then it is as you are saying it to be’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn abu ‘Abdallah in a marfu‘ manner has narrated from Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“O son of Adam, if a bird were to feed upon your heart, it would not satisfy its hunger. Only the eye of a needle, if placed over your eye, would be totally cover your vision.

With such (insignificant) means of perception how would you comprehend (Allah’s) vast dominion over the earth and the heavens? And if you think you can do so, there is the sun, one of creations of Allah. If your eyes can see the sun fully you then may think that you are right.”
